name: mount
synopsis: int mount(const char *source, const char *target, const char *filesystemtype, unsigned long mountflags, const void *_Nullable data);
description: The mount() system call attaches a filesystem specified by source to the directory or file specified by target. It requires appropriate privileges and can perform operations such as mounting, remounting, or binding based on the flags provided.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pathname of the filesystem to mount, such as a device, directory, file, or dummy string.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Pathname of the directory or file where the filesystem is to be attached.

parameters.name: filesystemtype
parameters.description: Type of the filesystem, e.g., 'ext4', as listed in /proc/filesystems.

parameters.name: mountflags
parameters.description: Flags that determine the mount operation and modify behavior, such as MS_REMOUNT or MS_BIND.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Filesystem-specific data, typically a string of comma-separated options, or NULL if no options are needed.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: A component of a path was not searchable.
Mounting a read-only filesystem was attempted without giving the MS_RDONLY flag.
The block device source is located on a filesystem mounted with the MS_NODEV option.
An attempt was made to stack a new mount directly on top of an existing mount point with the same source and target.
Source cannot be remounted read-only because it still holds files open for writing.
One of the pointer arguments points outside the user address space.
Source had an invalid superblock.
A remount operation (MS_REMOUNT) was attempted, but source was not already mounted on target.
A move operation (MS_MOVE) was attempted, but the mount tree under source includes unbindable mounts and target is a mount with propagation type MS_SHARED.
A move operation (MS_MOVE) was attempted, but the parent mount of source has propagation type MS_SHARED.
A move operation (MS_MOVE) was attempted, but source was not a mount, or was '/'.
A bind operation (MS_BIND) was requested where source referred to a mount namespace magic link and the propagation type of the parent mount of target was MS_SHARED.

Mount flags includes MS_SHARED, MS_PRIVATE, MS_SLAVE, or MS_UNBINDABLE and also includes a flag other than MS_REC or MS_SILENT.
